keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria draws 957 gazetteer cells (260,980 km2; bbox 84.2-90.9 E, 21.6-26.8 N: Bengal, eastern Bihar and the Jharkhand border) for 1534-1539 and calls it a separate polity. The Hussain Shahi page, however, gives the dynasty as the rulers of the Sultanate of Bengal ('from 1494 to 1538'), so the row is the same state as Cliopatria's own Sultanate of Bengal row (to 1533), whose 1529 shape holds 956 of these 957 cells. It is also not a different land: the page has Husain Shah conquering 'Kamrup-Kamata and Orissa' and extending the sultanate 'all the way to the port of Chittagong', none of which the shape contains (4 Odisha cells, 6 Assam cells, no Chittagong or Sylhet cells). The page gives no area and no boundary, so the infobox cannot be compared with Cliopatria's 260,980 km2. The years are also wrong at the end: the page has 'Deposition: 1538' and the Afghans under Sher Shah sacking the capital in 1538 (6 April 1538 on the Mahmud Shah page), so 1538 (April) to 1539 is the Sur Empire's Bengal, not this dynasty's. The corrected realm for 1534-1538 is drawn in the sultanate-of-bengal dossier as sultanate-of-bengal_1534 (base outline: Cliopatria's Sultanate of Bengal 1529 with Kamata, Sylhet, Chittagong and the Barh frontier handled there); do not draw both.

ledger.note: Page silent on 1534. The Hussain Shahi page dates the dynasty 'Founded: 1494' (founder Alauddin Husain Shah) and says it ruled the Sultanate of Bengal 'from 1494 to 1538'; the Mahmud Shah page has his reign 'from 1533 to 1538 CE'. The 1534 start is only Cliopatria's: its Sultanate of Bengal row ends in 1533 and this row begins a year later over the same land. This is therefore the start of a dynasty-labelled window of the sultanate-of-bengal state, not a founding; the dynasty's own founding in 1494 belongs to that dossier.

Cliopatria row 'Hussain Shahi Dynasty' 1534-1539, one shape of 957 gazetteer cells (260,980 km2). Verdict wrong, because the row is not a state of its own.
Merge or alias: the Hussain Shahi page says the dynasty ruled the Sultanate of Bengal 'from 1494 to 1538', so the row duplicates Cliopatria's Sultanate of Bengal (to 1533) and the sultanate-of-bengal dossier (sa-04-c), which runs 1342 to 6 April 1538 and has its own sultanate-of-bengal_1534 keyframe (1534-1538), the same Teliagarhi loss, the same 6 April 1538 dissolve and the same war. 956 of this shape's 957 cells lie inside Cliopatria's Bengal 1529 shape. Recommendation: merge hussain-shahi-dynasty into sultanate-of-bengal (keep the slug as an alias or a dynasty strip), or drop this slug from rendering. If both are drawn, Bengal appears twice in 1534-1538.
Years: Cliopatria runs to 1539; the dynasty ends on 6 April 1538 (Mahmud Shah page; Hussain Shahi page 'Deposition: 1538'). 1538 (April) to 1539 is the Sur Empire's Bengal (sur-empire_1538, 1538-1539, Humayun's seizure of Gauda on 8 September 1538 is in that dossier). The Cliopatria row is therefore too long by a year and a half.
Land: the page says Husain Shah 'conquered Kamrup-Kamata and Orissa' and extended the sultanate 'all the way to the port of Chittagong'. The Cliopatria shape holds 4 Odisha cells, 6 Assam cells and none of Chittagong or Sylhet; it does hold 252 of the 366 Bihar cells and 94 Jharkhand cells, so the Teliagarhi loss of 1536-37 is inside it. Whether Orissa and Kamata were still held in the 1530s is not on these two pages; the sultanate-of-bengal dossier covers the Kamata, Arakan (Chittagong) and Ahom questions.
Page conflicts: the Hussain Shahi page's infobox lists Gaur but its text says Mahmud Shah 'continued to rule from Sonargaon'; the Mahmud Shah page has 'his capital of Gaur was sacked'. Gaur is kept. The Mahmud Shah page also notes that 'the Portuguese arrived in Chittagong in 1534'; this moves no border (Chittagong lay with Arakan in the sultanate-of-bengal dossier) and is left out of the ledger.
Pages: two, both opened in this run; the budget was 1-2.
Gazetteer: the place 'Gaur' is not in places.jsonl (the capital uses lon/lat); the regions 'Bihar (region)', 'Sylhet (region)' and 'Chittagong (region)' resolve.
